questions.q: Is Ashgrove Components, the company in this closing case study, a real manufacturer?
options: No — like Lesson 29's Northfield Outfitters, it is explicitly fictional, invented to give the course one connected closing example
Yes, it is a real publicly traded company
Yes, but with its financial figures altered for confidentiality
The lesson leaves this ambiguous
questions.explain: The guide states plainly that Ashgrove Components is fictional and no figure in it is a real company's actual data.

questions.q: Which four dimensions did the Ashgrove finance team consider as possible explanations for the reconciliation break?
options: Accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and validity
Only accuracy — the other dimensions don't apply to financial data
Security, privacy, availability, and durability
Uniqueness, consistency, completeness, and accuracy
questions.explain: Each dimension pointed to a different plausible cause, which is why the team named all four before investigating further.

questions.q: What ultimately explained the 12 transactions that failed the referential integrity check?
options: They used a cost-center code that had been retired, which the ERP's GL posting job silently rejected instead of erroring loudly
They were entered twice by mistake
They were missing a customer ID
They were posted to the wrong fiscal year
questions.explain: A referential integrity check (Lesson 19 style) against the valid cost-center list flagged these 12 rows specifically.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause behind the validity failures, once 5 Whys was applied?
options: A process gap — a new product line's cost centers were added to the source system but never added to the GL posting job's reference table
A hardware failure in the ERP server
An intentional act of fraud by an employee
A database backup that restored outdated data
questions.explain: The lesson classifies this as a process root cause, not a technology bug — the reference table was manually maintained and missed an update.

questions.q: According to the lesson, which course does the Data Governance path continue with after Data Quality Management?
options: Metadata Management and Business Glossary
Data Visualization and EDA
Advanced Databricks
The path ends with this course
questions.explain: The outro and closing guide text both name Metadata Management and Business Glossary as the next course in the Data Governance path.
